sessions.title: Gym Strength, Hip Mobility #2 & Light Vault Tech
sessions.description: 55-minute gym session building directly on last Thursday's baseline. Warm-up (8 min): Easy indoor rowing focused on smooth technique—drive with legs first, hinge back slightly, then pull arms; reverse on recovery. Keep HR strictly <130 bpm (last week crept to 144 bpm). Strength Block (35 min): 1) Goblet Squat: 1 warm-up set of 10 reps at 4 kg, then 3x10 reps at 12 kg (adding the 3rd set you skipped last week; rest 90-120s between sets so quad burn stays manageable). 2) Dumbbell or Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x10 reps with very light load (2x8-10 kg dumbbells or an empty 20 kg bar). Focus 100% on a strict hip hinge: push hips straight back, keep a neutral/flat spine, slight knee bend, and stop the descent mid-shin before your lower back rounds. 3) Glute Bridge: 3x15 reps bodyweight with a 3-second squeeze at the top (progressing from 3x12 which felt easy). 4) Lat Pulldown: 1x12 at 35 kg, then 3x10 at 50 kg (upper-body pulling foundation for pole vault). 5) Core Circuit (3 rounds): Pallof Press 10 reps/side + Front Plank 35 seconds (brace glutes and abs hard). Optional playful pole vaulting technique drills for 10-12 min if desired, keeping takeoff impact conservative. Cool-down Mobility (12 min minimum—up from 2.5 min last week): 2x60s/side half-kneeling hip flexor stretch, 2x60s/side elevated single-leg hamstring stretch (hinge at hips with a flat back), and 2x45s/side figure-4 glute stretch.

sessions.title: Beginner Run/Walk Progression (Flat Terrain)
sessions.description: 30-minute easy beginner run/walk outdoors (use headlamp after work). Only run if your quads and calves feel fresh after Sunday's hike and Tuesday's goblet squats; if legs feel heavy, do a brisk flat walk instead. Structure: 5 min brisk walk warm-up, then 4 rounds of (4 min easy jog / 1 min walk), finishing with a 5 min cool-down walk. Keep cadence light and quick (~170 spm) with short strides to protect your lower back and build lower-limb tendon elasticity ahead of December's pole vault sprint prep. Cap HR strictly below 145 bpm (aim for 125-138 bpm during jog segments).

sessions.title: Steady Aerobic Indoor Ride (140-150 W)
sessions.description: 60-minute flat-effort indoor trainer ride to stimulate fat oxidation and aerobic efficiency without adding impact stress. Last Friday and Saturday you executed great flat HR lines averaging ~120-122 W; today we nudge the main block up slightly. Warm-up: 10 min building smoothly from 100 W to 135 W. Main set: 45 min steady at 140-150 W (ERG mode), cadence 85-95 rpm, keeping HR flat between 120-140 bpm. Cool-down: 5 min easy spin at 100-115 W. Practice rotating your pelvis slightly forward on the saddle (hinging from the hips rather than rounding the lumbar spine) for 5-minute blocks to take excess pressure off your sit bones.

sessions.title: Gym Strength & Hip Mobility #3 (Pre-Hike Cap)
sessions.description: 50-minute gym session kept deliberately conservative in lower-body volume so your legs have a full 48 hours to freshen up for Sunday's 5-hour mountain hike. Warm-up (8 min): Easy indoor rowing at 18-20 spm, HR <130 bpm, focusing on a tall posture and hip swing. Strength Block (27 min): 1) Goblet Squat: 3x10 reps at 12 kg (smooth, controlled tempo, no grinding). 2) Strict Dumbbell RDL: 3x10 reps at 2x10 kg (feel the stretch in the hamstrings while keeping your lower back locked in neutral—stop immediately if you feel any lumbar fatigue). 3) Seated Cable Row or Chest-Supported Row: 3x12 reps at moderate weight (40-45 kg) focusing on scapular control. 4) Core Anti-Extension/Anti-Rotation: 3x8/side Bird-Dog with a 3-sec hold + 3x10/side Pallof Press. Dedicated Mobility Block (15 min): Deep hip flexor, hamstring, and thoracic spine mobility work—aim to finish feeling looser and more energized than when you walked in.

sessions.title: Full Rest Day Ahead of 5-Hour Hike
sessions.description: True rest day—do not add an unplanned indoor ride today like last Saturday! Keeping today completely free of training load ensures your glycogen stores, postural muscles, and legs are ready for tomorrow's 5-hour mountain outing. Optional 10 minutes of gentle hip and lower-back stretching in the evening. Prepare your gear, clothing layers, headlamp (in case the hike runs near dusk), and steady hike nutrition (aim for simple snacks providing ~30-40g carbs per hour during the hike so you do not return home ravenous and overeat).

sessions.title: Long Endurance Mountain Hike
sessions.description: 5-hour steady mountain hike. This is the cornerstone endurance session of the week and a major fat-oxidation stimulus. Pacing discipline is critical: keep your average HR in the 115-135 bpm range and strictly cap steep uphill pitches at 145 bpm (unlike last Sunday where climbs pushed HR into the 150s-160s). Shorten your stride on steep gradients to protect your lower back and glutes. Keep summit or clothing stops brief (under 5-10 minutes) so you stay warm and maintain continuous aerobic demand. Eat small, regular snacks during the hike and have a balanced, protein-rich recovery meal waiting at home.

sessions.title: Gym Strength, Hip Mobility & Vault Tech 1
sessions.description: Warm-up: 5 min easy indoor rowing (keep HR < 130 bpm, focus on leg drive before leaning back). Strength Circuit (controlled tempo, stop immediately if lower back feels tired): 1) Goblet Squat: 1x10 @ 4 kg warm-up, then 3x10 @ 12 kg (rest 90s between sets). 2) Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x10 @ 8-10 kg per hand (strict hip hinge: unlock knees slightly, push hips straight back with a flat neutral spine until you feel a mild hamstring stretch—do NOT try to touch the floor). 3) Supine Glute Bridge: 3x12 with a 3-second squeeze at the top. 4) Lat Pulldown: 1x12 @ 35 kg, 2x10 @ 50 kg (great pull power transfer for pole vault). 5) Pallof Press: 3x10 per side. 6) Front Plank: 3x30s (rest 45s between sets). Finish with 10-12 min of playful pole vault drills/technique, followed by a mandatory 12-15 min of dedicated hip mobility (2 min per side kneeling hip-flexor couch stretch, 2 min per side elevated-hands hamstring hinge stretch, 2 min per side pigeon/figure-4 stretch).

sessions.title: Beginner Run/Walk Progression
sessions.description: Since the run/walk was replaced by the mountain hike on Oct 25, we start your running progression cleanly today. Head out with your headlamp. Perform a 5-minute brisk walk warm-up, then complete 5 rounds of: 4 minutes easy jogging / 1 minute walking (30 minutes total). Keep your cadence light and quick (~170+ spm) to minimize impact on your lower back and knees, and strictly cap HR below 140 bpm (mostly 120-135 bpm). If HR creeps over 140 bpm on hills, walk immediately.

sessions.title: Beginner Indoor Rowing & Hip Mobility
sessions.description: Session 1 of your beginner rowing program. Set the damper low (3-4, drag factor ~110-115) to protect your lower back. Focus entirely on stroke sequence: Drive = Legs -> Hips -> Arms; Recovery = Arms -> Hips (hinge forward from the pelvis, don't round the lumbar spine) -> Legs. Workout: 5 min easy warm-up row @ 18-20 strokes per minute (spm); then 4 x 4 minutes steady @ 20-22 spm with 90 seconds easy paddling or standing stretch rest between intervals; 3 min cool-down. Keep HR strictly between 120-138 bpm. Finish with 10 minutes of floor hip-flexor and hamstring stretching.

sessions.title: Steady Zone 2 Indoor Cycling
sessions.description: Building on your well-executed October 23 & 24 trainer rides (where you averaged ~122 W with a flat HR around 120 bpm), today we nudge power into the target Zone 2 band while keeping that exact same smooth, surge-free line. Warm-up: 10 min progressive from 100 W to 135 W. Main set: 45 min steady in ERG mode (or flat virtual road) at 135-150 W, cadence 85-95 rpm, keeping HR between 120-138 bpm. Cool-down: 5 min easy spin at 100 W. Periodically practice tilting your pelvis slightly forward (hinging from the hips rather than rounding the lower back) to unload your sit bones.

sessions.title: Gym Strength, Posterior Chain & Vault Tech 2
sessions.description: Warm-up: 5 min easy incline treadmill walk or staircase machine (HR < 130 bpm). Strength Circuit: 1) Goblet Squat: 3x10 @ 12-14 kg (if Tuesday's 3x10 @ 12 kg felt controlled without heavy quad burn, move to 14 kg). 2) Dumbbell RDL: 3x10 @ 10-12 kg per hand (slow 3-second lowering phase, stop just below the knees, keep spine completely neutral). 3) Single-Leg Glute Bridge (or Feet-Elevated Bridge): 3x10 per side. 4) Seated Cable Row: 3x12 @ 40-45 kg (squeeze shoulder blades, keep torso upright). 5) Deadbug or Bird-Dog: 3x10 per side (slow, controlled lumbar stability). 6) Farmer's Carry: 3x40m @ 16-20 kg per hand (great core bracing). Include 10-12 min of pole vault technical work/drills and 12-15 min of deep hip-flexor, glute, and hamstring mobility.

Choose a rolling trail or mountain route for a 1h45 hike (or take the fatbike/studded gravel bike if you prefer riding). Discipline rule: use short steps on steep climbs to keep HR strictly under 140 bpm (aim for 115-135 bpm average, no 160+ bpm surges) and keep any summit stop under 5 minutes so you stay warm and maintain continuous aerobic stimulus.

tomorrow.title: Gym Strength, Hip Mobility & Vault Tech 1
tomorrow.description: Warm-up: 5 min easy indoor rowing (keep HR < 130 bpm, focus on leg drive before leaning back). Strength Circuit (controlled tempo, stop immediately if lower back feels tired): 1) Goblet Squat: 1x10 @ 4 kg warm-up, then 3x10 @ 12 kg (rest 90s between sets). 2) Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL): 3x10 @ 8-10 kg per hand (strict hip hinge: unlock knees slightly, push hips straight back with a flat neutral spine until you feel a mild hamstring stretch—do NOT try to touch the floor). 3) Supine Glute Bridge: 3x12 with a 3-second squeeze at the top. 4) Lat Pulldown: 1x12 @ 35 kg, 2x10 @ 50 kg (great pull power transfer for pole vault). 5) Pallof Press: 3x10 per side. 6) Front Plank: 3x30s (rest 45s between sets). Finish with 10-12 min of playful pole vault drills/technique, followed by a mandatory 12-15 min of dedicated hip mobility (2 min per side kneeling hip-flexor couch stretch, 2 min per side elevated-hands hamstring hinge stretch, 2 min per side pigeon/figure-4 stretch).
alternatives: If 12 kg goblet squats still cause heavy quad burn on set 2, drop to 8-10 kg for the 3rd set so your lower back doesn't take over.
tomorrow.rationale: This session directly builds on your October 22 gym baseline. In that session, you wisely stopped at 2 sets of 12 kg goblet squats and skipped deadlifts due to quad fatigue, and only managed 2.5 minutes of stretching. Tomorrow we add the 3rd goblet squat set, introduce very light, strict Dumbbell RDLs to teach your hamstrings and glutes to share the load with your lower back, and expand hip stretching to a dedicated 12-15 minutes alongside your pole vault technical work.
tomorrow.optionalRationale: This session builds the posterior-chain durability, lumbar anti-rotation stability, and pelvic anterior tilt range of motion needed to stop lower-back pain on climbs, eliminate sit-bone blisters during your 2027 brevets and Paris-Brest-Paris, and protect your spine during the explosive takeoff of the January 7 Pole Vault Championship. Skipping it delays your structural progression and leaves your lower back vulnerable when dynamic vault loading begins in December.
